originality.rationale: A best-knowledge, qualified novelty assessment of the conditional exchangeability theorem, NOT of the deterministic weighted-cycle gambler’s-ruin formula. Full accessible recent motivating primary text distinguishes homogeneous/time-inhomogeneous models and explicitly raises random spatial environments. The much closer Mosbah–Saheb (2000) abstract says it computes a general fixed-environment last-vertex probability; those fixed-environment ingredients are acknowledged and possibly dominated. The additional universality given the complete unordered random edge multiset is a separate quantified stochastic assertion obtained by conditional permutation symmetrization and not identified in available prior statements. Its complete 2000 text was inaccessible; the priority risk is material and remains outstanding.
residual_risks: Mosbah–Saheb 2000 already supplies general deterministic weighted-cycle probability formulas; unread full text may contain or transparently imply the symmetrized result. This is a substantive, not merely formal, priority risk.

value.rationale: The distribution of the final discovered vertex is the natural coverage-fairness statistic singled out by a 2026 cycle-walk study and its random-site-parameter future direction. A single frozen inhomogeneous reversible environment usually has strongly nonuniform last-vertex probabilities, yet *every* arbitrary fully exchangeable edge assignment, even with strong dependence, restores uniformity conditional on the entire unordered list of edge weights. Conditional independence from a complete environmental sufficient statistic is a structural invariance stronger than expectation alone; the exact one-edge defect shows why it is not the ordinary unweighted-cycle deduction. Broader coverage via pre-existing weighted-cycle formulas is a residual scientific significance and priority risk.
